prompts: Separate project judgment from delivery mechanics. launcher.launch(task) should validate nonempty id and owner, then return a delivery receipt for any task kind/project without choosing priority or eligibility. Keep both mechanical validations. Put the health frequency and triage decisions in playbook.json as guidance entries named health-frequency and health-triage, rather than executable launcher rules.
A new project also uses this launcher. It must accept a research task just as it accepts health work, without project-specific branches. Leave the task object unchanged.

files.README.md: The project manager decides whether/when health work is useful and how failures become follow-up issues. The launcher only validates delivery identity and returns {delivered: task.id, owner: task.owner}.

checks.name: independent-outcome

rubric: Project health judgment belongs in one playbook; generic launcher code retains identity/delivery invariants and accepts different task kinds without mutation or hidden eligibility decisions.
provenance: claude-audit:agent-policy-not-dispatch-code; sanitized incident reconstruction using designed local fixtures, not a historical workspace replay; follow-up turns are designed extensions.
